entities.name: Primidone
observations: Primidone overdose can cause severe barbiturate toxicity through its active phenobarbital metabolite.
Source scenario: patient uses primidone for essential tremor and presents with coma, hypothermia, respiratory depression, hypotension, sluggish pupils, and hyporeflexia.

entities.name: Phenobarbital
observations: Phenobarbital is an active primidone metabolite and produces coma, hypothermia, respiratory depression, hypotension, sluggish pupils, and hyporeflexia in severe poisoning.
Urinary alkalinization can enhance renal elimination because phenobarbital is a weak acid, but it is adjunctive and does not replace airway support.
Multiple-dose activated charcoal may enhance phenobarbital clearance; extracorporeal removal is reserved for massive or refractory poisoning.

entities.name: Barbiturate overdose airway support
observations: In severe primidone/phenobarbital poisoning with coma and shallow inadequate respirations, immediate endotracheal intubation and assisted ventilation are indicated; there is no routine specific antidote.

entities.name: Phenobarbital urinary alkalinization
observations: Intravenous sodium bicarbonate for urinary alkalinization may be considered as an adjunct in significant phenobarbital poisoning, targeting urine pH above approximately 7.5, but it does not substitute for ventilatory support.
